{{Short description|Arawakan language spoken in Peru}} {{Infobox language | name = Axininca | nativename = | states = [[Peru]] | speakers = 4,000 | date = 2000 | ref = e18 | familycolor = arawakan | fam1 = [[Maipurean languages|Arawakan]] | fam2 = Southern | fam3 = [[Campa languages|Campa]] (Pre-Andine) | iso3 = cpc | glotto = ajyi1238 | glottorefname = Ajyininka Apurucayali | notice = IPA | altname = Ajyéninka | pronunciation = {{IPA|[aˈçiniŋka]}} }} '''Axininca''' (also "''Axininca Campa''"'',''{{Efn|The name ''Campa'' is offensive.}} ''Ajyíninka Apurucayali, Campa, Ashaninca, Ashéninca Apurucayali, Apurucayali Campa, Ajyéninka'') is an [[Arawakan language]] of the [[Ashéninka language|Ashéninka]] dialect group spoken along the [[Apurucayali River|Apurucayali]] tributary of the [[Pachitea River]] in [[Peru]]. It has figured prominently in formal linguistic theory involving [[phonology]] (especially [[Prosody (linguistics)|prosody]] including its [[stress (linguistics)|stress]]) and [[morphology (linguistics)|morphology]] (Black 1991; Casali 1996, 2011; De Lacy 2002, 2006; De Lacy & Kingston 2013; Itô 1986, 1989; Levin 1985; Lombardi 2002; McCarthy & Prince 1993; Morley 2015; Rosenthall & Horn 1997; Spring 1990a, 1990b, 1990c, 1992; Yip 1983). ==Demographics and language policy== There is 20% literacy in Ajyíninka Apurucayali and 30% literacy in Spanish; there was 40 to 50% bilingualism between the two as of 1981. ==Phonology== ===Consonants=== Payne (1981) describes the following Axininca consonant inventory:{{cite book |last1=Payne |first1=David L. |url=https://www.sil.org/system/files/reapdata/45/00/78/45007820652756325382028963373179747048/16298.pdf |title=The Phonology and Morphology of Axininca Campa |date=1981 |publisher=Summer Institute of Linguistics |location=Dallas}} {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: center" |- ! colspan="2" | ! However, pronouns and adverbs, as well as adjectives and nouns, are morphologically identical to each other. Verb stems cannot occur isolated. Nouns and adjectives may be suffixed for possession. Adverbs and pronouns can occur in isolation, but cannot take possessive affixes. ==Notes== {{Notelist}} == References == {{reflist}} ==Bibliography== * Black, H Andrew. (1991).
